production.note: US model years. KBB's F12berlinetta listing is headed 2017 and links model years '2016', '2015', '2014' and '2013'. Evo: 'Built to replace the 599 GTB in 2012, the F12 was on sale for five years until it was succeeded by the 812 Superfast' (evo-f12), titling it '(2012-2017)' (calendar years; unveiled at Geneva in March 2012 per the Ferrari release reproduced by Autoblog). The open F12 variants (F60America) and the F12tdf are separate cars.

body.note: Two-seat front-engined V12 berlinetta; no open version of this variant.

configuration.note: Ferrari release as reproduced by Autoblog: '65-degree V12'

displacementL.note: 6,262 cc. Ferrari specification as printed by Just Cars: 'Total displacement 6262 cc' (justcars-f12); Top Gear: 'V12, 6262cc, 65 degree vee angle' (topgear-f12).

fuel.note: Petrol V12 with no hybrid system; inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Top Gear: '730bhp through the rear wheels'

transmission.note: Evo: 'All that mumbo is transmitted to the 315-section rear tyres via a 7-speed dual clutch transaxle and Ferrari's E-Diff.' Ferrari's release (autoblog-f12-release) calls it the 'F1 dual-clutch transmission'. No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 740 cv x 0.98632 = 729.9, rounded to 730 hp. Quote (Ferrari release of 29 February 2012 as reproduced by Autoblog): "Maximum power output 740 CV at 8500 rpm" (reproduced on a second request). Evo's and Top Gear's panels print the same 730bhp (Evo: 'Power | 730bhp'). KBB's US listing shows '740 @ 8250 RPM', the metric number. No separate SAE rating published by Ferrari for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: 1,630 kg x 2.20462 = 3,593.5, rounded to 3,594 lb. Coupe with the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only configuration). Quote (Evo specification panel): "Weight | 1630kg" (unlabelled; Evo marks dry figures as dry elsewhere). Top Gear calls the same figure the kerb weight: "kerbweight of 1630kg" (topgear-f12). Ferrari gives only a dry weight: "Dry weight* 1525 kg" (autoblog-f12-release); Ferrari's specification as printed by Just Cars (justcars-f12, Mike Ryan, 2 December 2012) gives the footnote: "*With lightweight options". 1,630 kg is exactly 105 kg above that optioned dry weight, so it is treated as step 3 of the weight order (an optioned car's curb weight): no standard-car curb weight was found, and a standard car is somewhat heavier. KBB's US listing shows '3594 lbs.' (kbb-f12).

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs kerb. Ferrari's release lists only a dry weight; Evo's panel and Top Gear give 1,630 kg, 105 kg more.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the published kerb figure under weight step 3 (very probably an optioned car), since no standard-car curb weight was found and a curb weight ranks above a dry weight.
